transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-08
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Omar Singh (Redwood SE), Lina Park (Redwood Solutions), Raj Patel (CTO - Atlas), Sofia Martinez (Head of ML), Tom Reed (Infra Lead), Priya Nair (Security)

Summary (auto):
- POC scoping to decide between Hosted, Dedicated, or Private deployment for Atlas Retail's recommendation engine and personalization infra.
- Discussed success criteria (latency, throughput, cost per 1k requests), benchmark plan, data residency & compliance needs, timeline for a 6-week POC and next steps.

Topics: success criteria, workload sizing, benchmarks, hosted vs dedicated vs private decision criteria, security/compliance needs, timeline and next steps

[00:00] Maya: ok, thanks everyone for joining, um, quick intros then we'll dive into current load and goals.
[00:18] Raj: hey all, Raj here, CTO at Atlas. Thanks for setting this up. Sofia will walk through ML requirements, Tom will cover infra, and Priya will cover security.
[00:28] Sofia: hi everyone, our rec system serves personalization across web and mobile. We're currently doing a hybrid -- some models hosted on vendor A, some on-prem for PII-sensitive flows, trying to move to a more unified inference layer.
[00:45] Omar: great, curious about peak qps, latency SLOs and payload sizes?
[00:52] Tom: peaks are about 1k qps for product listing pages during promotions, average p99 latency target is 120-200 ms for model-only inference, end-to-end not including network. Payloads are small, ~600 bytes avg, but some multi-turn context for session-scoring goes to ~3 KB.
[01:15] Sofia: model sizes range; main production model is a 7B transformer, a few smaller 2B models for personalization variants. We also experiment with an LLM-based reranker that needs streaming support.
[01:34] Maya: ok so three main asks: throughput/latency, cost predictability, and strict data residency for user PII. Is that fair?
[01:44] Priya: yes and audit logs, KMS integration, and SSO/SAML for user access - SOC2 posture is a must, plus some EU data residency requirements.
[01:55] Omar: noted. quick note on the deployment modes — Hosted gives fastest onboarding and lower ops, Dedicated is reserved GPU pools with consistent throughput, and Private (VPC/on-prem) gives the most control but more ops. We'll walk through tradeoffs with your numbers.
[02:12] Raj: we're leaning away from full private unless necessary because ops headcount is limited, but data residency + compliance may force parts to be private or VPC.
[02:24] Sofia: timeline-wise we want a POC in July, aiming to evaluate within 4-6 weeks and decide before Q4 procurement.

-- Workload sizing and benchmarks --
[02:45] Omar: based on 1k peak qps and a 7B model, typical token length distribution is 50-150 tokens; cost and latency vary a lot with batch size and quantization. For Hosted we can recommend a standard config to hit ~150 ms p50 and ~220 ms p99 for the 7B using batching + KV caching.
[03:10] Tom: what's the expected cost per 1k requests in hosted assumptions?
[03:16] Maya: rough hosted estimate for 7B w/ caching is $X per 1k, we'll send exact SKU numbers; but dedicated can lower per-token costs by 30-50% depending on commit and utilization.
[03:28] Raj: that makes sense, the cost delta is important. Our CFO wants to see committed vs variable numbers.
[03:35] Omar: also note Dedicated gives you reserved capacity and predictable throughput, plus the ability to control model variants and quant profiles. Private gives full control of network, KMS, and we can integrate with HSM but you manage the infra.

-- Security & compliance discussion --
[04:00] Priya: for private/VPC we need to ensure KMS integration and audit logs with 1-year retention; also need SOC2 artifact examples, pen test summaries.
[04:12] Lina: we can provide SOC2 reports, penetration test summary, and a security pack. For KMS we support customer-managed keys and HSM integrations for Private and Dedicated options.
[04:28] Priya: ok, what about data residency for EU users? we need EU-only processing for certain flows.
[04:34] Maya: Hosted supports region pinning (EU regions) for the hosted API, Dedicated can be provisioned in EU capacity, Private obviously can be fully in your EU VPC.

-- Decision criteria conversation --
[04:50] Omar: so map the decision to three axes: cost (unit economics), ops overhead, and compliance/residency. If compliance/residency is non-negotiable for core flows, Private or Dedicated VPC is likely. If you want lower ops and faster time-to-value, Hosted. If you want both predictability and reduced ops compared to Private, Dedicated is a middle ground.
[05:12] Raj: would Dedicated let us burst to additional capacity during peak promos?
[05:18] Omar: yes, Dedicated has burst policies and autoscale options; you can configure baseline reserved capacity plus burst credits.
[05:25] Tom: curious about canary rollouts and model versioning — we need easy rollback if quality regressions happen.
[05:31] Lina: the Redwood Console supports canary deploys, A/B, and automated fallback to a compatible variant. We also do per-route metrics and token-level cost breakdowns.

-- Benchmarks and POC plan --
[05:50] Maya: proposed POC: 4-6 weeks. Week 0: onboarding and instrumentation; Week 1-2: run baseline hosted benchmarks with your sample traffic; Week 3: run dedicated config benchmark (if you choose); Week 4-5: analysis and quality evals, rollback checks, SLA verification.
[06:12] Sofia: for benchmarks we'll provide sample payloads and a 24-hour replay of a promotion spike. We'll need guidance on metrics to collect.
[06:22] Omar: benchmark checklist we'll send includes p50/p90/p99 latency, throughput, token cost, txn error rate, and quality regression tests using your eval prompts. We'll also include KV cache hit-rate metrics.
[06:35] Raj: what about streaming for reranker? we need less than 300 ms for first byte ideally.
[06:40] Omar: streaming support is available on Hosted and Dedicated; Private depends on networking but should be fine. We can include streaming in the benchmark scripts.

-- Objections and tradeoffs --
[06:55] Raj: primary objections from procurement are vendor lock and long-term cost.
[07:00] Maya: we recommend staged commitments — start Hosted POC to validate function, then move to Dedicated with a 6-12 month commit for cost savings if utilization justifies. Private usually reserved for strong compliance needs.
[07:14] Priya: data retention and ability to delete user data on request is a must. How does Redwood handle DSRs?
[07:21] Lina: we log data lineage and can support deletion requests; for Hosted we have retention controls, Dedicated and Private give you more control over storage retention. We'll include details in security pack.

-- Questions from Atlas --
[07:35] Tom: can we run custom kernels or quant profiles on Dedicated?
[07:40] Omar: yes, Dedicated supports configurable quantization profiles and kernel selection; for Private we can enable it but some ops involvement is required.
[07:48] Sofia: any limits on concurrent streams or request shapes?
[07:52] Omar: no hard limits, it's more about the capacity you provision; we'll simulate your shapes in the benchmark.

-- Recap and next steps --
[08:10] Maya: recap: we'll send pricing/SKU, security pack, and benchmark scripts. Atlas to provide sample payloads and SLOs. We'll schedule benchmarking week of Jul 20. POC target 4-6 weeks.
[08:25] Raj: sounds good. can we get a one-pager that maps decision criteria to recommendation?
[08:30] Maya: yes, we'll include a decision matrix: Hosted if you prioritize time-to-value and lower ops; Dedicated for predictable throughput and cost savings with moderate ops; Private for strict compliance/residency needs.
[08:42] Priya: please include explicit KMS/HSM integration notes and SOC2 artefacts.
[08:47] Lina: will do.
[08:50] Sofia: thanks all, we'll chat after we collect payloads.
